rounds.text: Taylormade Renewables Ltd trades at a price-to-book ratio of just 0.75x, sitting well below the sector benchmark of 2.32x, which indicates a tangible asset discount relative to peers [E2, E7]. The business maintains a conservative balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.19x as of September 2026, alongside manageable borrowings that have actually decreased year-on-year from Rs 21.25 Cr to Rs 20.66 Cr [E26, E28]. Short-term liquidity is comfortable backed by a current ratio of 2.46x as of March 2026 [E27]. Operational metrics show notable green shoots, including a significant improvement in debtor days from 232 down to 159 days, and recent screening highlights explosive revenue expansion with sales jumping 549% year-on-year alongside a 17% increase in net profit [E40, E46, E48]. Furthermore, results are accelerating with a high results score of 85 out of 100, proving that recent performance is turning around ahead of market expectations [E36, E54]. Conceded: [E14], [E24], [E25], [E32], [E42].

Taylormade Renewables Ltd carries significant valuation and operational risks, evidenced by a discounted cash flow model pinning intrinsic value at just Rs 31 per share against a market price of Rs 67, resulting in a severe -113.1% margin of safety [E32, E33]. The current market price demands an unrealistic 20.5% earnings growth rate, vastly outstripping the 10.0% assumed in the base case [E34]. Operational fundamentals lag far behind sector benchmarks, with a depressed ROE of 1.82% and ROCE of 3.21% compared to sector medians of 11.24% and 12.9% respectively [E9, E10]. Cash generation is deeply compromised, reflected in a negative operating cash flow of Rs -8.44 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs -11.22 Cr for March 2026, leading to a dismal cash conversion ratio of -4.64x [E23, E24, E25]. Furthermore, operating margins have experienced a catastrophic collapse of 30 percentage points over three years down to 5% in the TTM, accompanied by a continuous four-year downward trend [E20, E21]. Compounded share price performance mirrors these fundamental weaknesses, declining 52% over one year and 53% over three years while promoters steadily reduced their stake by 7.64 percentage points since May 2023 [E17, E18, E30]. conceded: [E26, E28, E46].

The bear's reliance on the discounted cash flow model at Rs 31 is overly rigid against concrete positive operational catalysts, notably that sales surged 549% year-on-year and net profit expanded by 17% [E32, E46, E48]. Furthermore, results are demonstrably improving with a score of 85 out of 100, proving that stale sentiment and backward-looking DCF assumptions miss the active fundamental turnaround [E54]. While the bear highlights lagging asset returns, debtor days have actively improved from 232 to 159 days, and the company is explicitly expected to deliver a good quarter [E40, E39]. The asset backing provides a firm margin of safety given that the stock trades at 0.75 times its book value of ₹ 89.6 against a sector benchmark P/B of 2.32x [E2, E7, E38]. Conceded: [E24, E25, E34].

The bull’s reliance on surging year-on-year sales [E46] ignores the trailing twelve month reality where compounded sales growth is actually -3% and compounded profit growth is -6% [E14, E15]. Conceded: [E48]. While the bull points to an improving results score of 85 out of 100 [E54], this operational uptick clashes with severe structural deterioration: operating margins have collapsed by 30 percentage points over three years from 36% down to 5% [E20], with both yearly and quarterly operating margin trends continuously decreasing [E21, E22]. The bull’s emphasis on improving debtor days from 232 to 159 days [E40] glosses over the fact that 159 days remains objectively high [E43], directly contributing to catastrophic cash burn where operating cash flow sits at negative Rs 8.44 Cr and free cash flow at negative Rs 11.22 Cr for March 2026 [E24, E25]. Furthermore, the bull’s argument that book value of ₹ 89.6 offers a firm margin of safety [E2] is invalidated by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 31 [E32] and a negative margin of safety of -113.1% [E33], meaning today's price already aggressively prices in 20.5% earnings growth [E34] while the company struggles with low return on equity at 1.9% to 2% [E13, E19, E50] and a low interest coverage ratio [E42].
